name: Bromelain

lead: Bromelain is a mixture of protein-digesting enzymes extracted mainly from pineapple stem. It is sold as a supplement and used in food processing; a topical form is approved for debriding burn wounds.
In appearance contexts it is used to reduce post-procedure swelling and bruising (for example after cosmetic surgery) and general inflammation. Study results are mixed and often small.

paras: Bromelain's proteolytic activity is thought to modulate inflammatory mediators such as bradykinin and prostaglandins and to affect fibrin breakdown. How much active enzyme survives digestion and reaches tissue after oral dosing is uncertain.

Side effects include stomach upset and allergic reactions, especially in people allergic to pineapple. It may increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants and interact with some antibiotics. Supplement potency is inconsistent. Legal as a supplement.
